source.title: When simulations look right but causal effects go wrong: Large language models as behavioral simulators
source.version: arXiv 2604.02458v1; preprint; HTML compilation date and arXiv date differ

study.population: Model predictions compared with human climate-intervention experiments
study.sample_unit: human records reported for the main benchmark

claim: Improved descriptive fit did not reliably imply improved causal-effect prediction.

outcome.name: Descriptive prediction error versus error in experimental treatment effects

findings.name: GPT-4o-mini baseline mean absolute ATE error
findings.locator: Results: Descriptive fit does not guarantee causal fidelity

limitations: Not a new randomized trial of Manager.
Lightweight models, no fine-tuning, and climate-domain scope limit generalization.
Reported sample differs from the original climate tournament; reconciliation remains open.
Numeric results are author reports, not independently rerun here.
